title: Our warming planet
paragraphs: We are all aware of climate change and how it is threatening our planet. Industrialisation, our disposable culture and population growth are some of the reasons why we are seeing average temperatures rise and more extreme weather events. And scientists are finding more evidence that the situation is getting worse.

The rise in global temperatures is the most important thing that experts analyse. They say keeping it below 1.5 centigrade will avoid the worst climate impacts. But The World Meteorological Organisation says there’s a 20% possibility the critical mark will be broken in any one year before 2024 – and there’s a 70% chance it will be broken in one or more months in those five years.

This isn’t great news for the Arctic, where the impact will be greatest: warming by twice the global average this year. Temperatures in the Siberian Arctic reached record averages in June – one area reached more than 30℃. This heat helped to fan wildfires, which in turn released 59 million tonnes of carbon dioxide. Meanwhile, in Western Europe, experts predict over the next five years rising sea levels will cause more storms.

But these events should not surprise us. Professor Martin Siegert from Imperial College London told the BBC this is “in line with predictions of global warming going back decades now. We don’t really need further confirmation of this problem, but here it is anyway.” He thinks if you change the weather in the Arctic you are likely to see the effects ripple out around the world.

We know that carbon emissions from human activities is partly to blame for our warming planet, but it seems measures to reduce this are not having much effect. The BBC’s Justin Rowlatt writing about the effects of events in the Arctic, says: “Climate scientists simply don’t know for certain what those effects are likely to be, but climate models suggest they will lead to more extreme weather events – heatwaves and severe storms.”

vocabulary.entry: climate change /ˈklaɪmət tʃeɪndʒ/ n. 气候变化
vocabulary.example: Climate change is a major threat to biodiversity.
vocabulary.translation: 气候变化是对生物多样性的重大威胁。

vocabulary.entry: industrialisation /ɪnˌdʌstriəlaɪˈzeɪʃn/ n. 工业化
vocabulary.example: The country's industrialisation began in the early 20th century.
vocabulary.translation: 这个国家的工业化始于20世纪初。

vocabulary.entry: disposable culture /dɪˈspəʊzəbl ˈkʌltʃə/ n. 一次性消费文化
vocabulary.example: Disposable culture has led to a lot of plastic waste.
vocabulary.translation: 一次性消费文化造成了大量的塑料垃圾。

vocabulary.entry: population growth /ˌpɒpjuˈleɪʃn ɡrəʊθ/ n. 人口增长
vocabulary.example: Rapid population growth has put pressure on natural resources.
vocabulary.translation: 人口的快速增长给自然资源带来了压力。

vocabulary.entry: average temperature /ˈævərɪdʒ ˈtemprətʃə/ n. 平均气温
vocabulary.example: The average temperature in July is higher than that in June.
vocabulary.translation: 七月的平均气温比六月高。

vocabulary.entry: extreme weather event /ɪkˈstriːm ˈweðə ɪˈvent/ n. 极端天气事件
vocabulary.example: Floods and droughts are common extreme weather events.
vocabulary.translation: 洪水和干旱是常见的极端天气事件。

vocabulary.entry: global temperature /ˈɡləʊbl ˈtemprətʃə/ n. 全球气温
vocabulary.example: Global temperature has been rising steadily over the past century.
vocabulary.translation: 过去一个世纪以来，全球气温一直在稳步上升。

vocabulary.entry: climate impact /ˈklaɪmət ˈɪmpækt/ n. 气候影响
vocabulary.example: We need to take action to reduce the climate impact of human activities.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要采取行动，减少人类活动对气候的影响。

vocabulary.entry: World Meteorological Organisation /ˈwɜːld ˌmiːtiərəˈlɒdʒɪkl ˌɔːɡənaɪˈzeɪʃn/ n. 世界气象组织
vocabulary.example: The World Meteorological Organisation provides weather forecasts worldwide.
vocabulary.translation: 世界气象组织提供全球范围的天气预报。

vocabulary.entry: critical mark /ˈkrɪtɪkl mɑːk/ n. 临界值
vocabulary.example: Scientists are monitoring whether the river level will reach the critical mark.
vocabulary.translation: 科学家们正在监测河水水位是否会达到临界值。

vocabulary.entry: Arctic /ˈɑːktɪk/ n. 北极地区
vocabulary.example: Polar bears live in the Arctic.
vocabulary.translation: 北极熊生活在北极地区。

vocabulary.entry: record average /ˈrekɔːd ˈævərɪdʒ/ n. 历史平均纪录
vocabulary.example: The city set a new record average temperature last winter.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市去年冬天创下了新的平均气温纪录。

vocabulary.entry: fan wildfire /fæn ˈwaɪldfaɪə/ v. 助长野火
vocabulary.example: Strong winds continued to fan wildfire in the forest.
vocabulary.translation: 强风持续助长着森林里的野火。

vocabulary.entry: carbon dioxide /ˈkɑːbən daɪˈɒksaɪd/ n. 二氧化碳
vocabulary.example: Burning fossil fuels releases large amounts of carbon dioxide.
vocabulary.translation: 燃烧化石燃料会释放大量的二氧化碳。

vocabulary.entry: sea level /siː ˈlevl/ n. 海平面
vocabulary.example: Rising sea level threatens coastal cities.
vocabulary.translation: 海平面上升对沿海城市构成威胁。

vocabulary.entry: in line with /ɪn laɪn wɪð/ 符合；与……一致
vocabulary.example: His actions are in line with his words.
vocabulary.translation: 他言行一致。

vocabulary.entry: global warming /ˈɡləʊbl ˈwɔːmɪŋ/ n. 全球变暖
vocabulary.example: Global warming has become a hot topic around the world.
vocabulary.translation: 全球变暖已成为全球热议的话题。

vocabulary.entry: confirmation /ˌkɒnfəˈmeɪʃn/ n. 证实；确认
vocabulary.example: We are waiting for confirmation of the news.
vocabulary.translation: 我们正在等待这条消息的证实。

vocabulary.entry: ripple out /ˈrɪpl aʊt/ 波及；扩散
vocabulary.example: The effects of the economic crisis rippled out to all sectors.
vocabulary.translation: 经济危机的影响波及到了所有行业。

vocabulary.entry: carbon emission /ˈkɑːbən ɪˈmɪʃn/ n. 碳排放
vocabulary.example: Many countries are making laws to cut carbon emission.
vocabulary.translation: 许多国家正在制定法律以减少碳排放。

vocabulary.entry: climate model /ˈklaɪmət ˈmɒdl/ n. 气候模型
vocabulary.example: Climate models are used to predict future weather patterns.
vocabulary.translation: 气候模型被用于预测未来的天气模式。

vocabulary.entry: heatwave /ˈhiːtweɪv/ n. 热浪
vocabulary.example: The heatwave lasted for two weeks and caused many heat-related illnesses.
vocabulary.translation: 热浪持续了两周，引发了许多与高温相关的疾病。

sentences.english: We are all aware of climate change and how it is threatening our planet.
sentences.chinese: 我们都深知气候变化的存在，也清楚它正威胁着我们的星球。

sentences.english: Industrialisation, our disposable culture and population growth are some of the reasons why we are seeing average temperatures rise and more extreme weather events.
sentences.chinese: 工业化发展、一次性消费文化以及人口增长，都是导致全球平均气温上升、极端天气事件频发的部分原因。

sentences.english: And scientists are finding more evidence that the situation is getting worse.
sentences.chinese: 而且科学家们还在不断发现新的证据，表明情况正在持续恶化。

sentences.english: The rise in global temperatures is the most important thing that experts analyse.
sentences.chinese: 全球气温上升是专家们分析的重中之重。

sentences.english: They say keeping it below 1.5 centigrade will avoid the worst climate impacts.
sentences.chinese: 他们表示，将气温升幅控制在1.5摄氏度以内，就能避免气候变化带来的最严重影响。

sentences.english: But The World Meteorological Organisation says there’s a 20% possibility the critical mark will be broken in any one year before 2024 – and there’s a 70% chance it will be broken in one or more months in those five years.
sentences.chinese: 但世界气象组织指出，2024年之前的任意一年，气温升幅突破这一临界值的概率为20%；而在这五年期间，至少有一个月突破该临界值的概率高达70%。

sentences.english: This isn’t great news for the Arctic, where the impact will be greatest: warming by twice the global average this year.
sentences.chinese: 这对北极地区而言绝非好消息，该地区受到的影响将最为严重：今年北极的升温速度是全球平均水平的两倍。

sentences.english: Temperatures in the Siberian Arctic reached record averages in June – one area reached more than 30℃.
sentences.chinese: 六月，西伯利亚北极地区的平均气温创下历史新高，其中有一片区域的气温甚至超过了30摄氏度。

sentences.english: This heat helped to fan wildfires, which in turn released 59 million tonnes of carbon dioxide.
sentences.chinese: 高温助长了野火的蔓延，这些野火转而释放出5900万吨二氧化碳。

sentences.english: Meanwhile, in Western Europe, experts predict over the next five years rising sea levels will cause more storms.
sentences.chinese: 与此同时，专家预测未来五年内，西欧地区的海平面上升将引发更多风暴。

sentences.english: But these events should not surprise us.
sentences.chinese: 但这些现象其实并不出人意料。

sentences.english: Professor Martin Siegert from Imperial College London told the BBC this is “in line with predictions of global warming going back decades now.
sentences.chinese: 伦敦帝国理工学院的马丁·西格特教授向英国广播公司表示，这“与数十年前关于全球变暖的预测完全吻合。

sentences.english: We don’t really need further confirmation of this problem, but here it is anyway.”
sentences.chinese: 我们其实并不需要更多证据来证实这个问题，但事实还是摆在了眼前。”

sentences.english: He thinks if you change the weather in the Arctic you are likely to see the effects ripple out around the world.
sentences.chinese: 他认为，一旦北极的气候模式发生改变，其影响很可能会波及全球。

sentences.english: We know that carbon emissions from human activities is partly to blame for our warming planet, but it seems measures to reduce this are not having much effect.
sentences.chinese: 我们都知道，人类活动产生的碳排放是地球变暖的部分原因，但目前来看，减排措施的效果并不明显。

sentences.english: The BBC’s Justin Rowlatt writing about the effects of events in the Arctic, says: “Climate scientists simply don’t know for certain what those effects are likely to be, but climate models suggest they will lead to more extreme weather events – heatwaves and severe storms.”
sentences.chinese: 英国广播公司的贾斯汀·罗莱特在撰文分析北极地区气候变化的影响时指出：“气候科学家们尚无法确切判断这些影响具体会是什么，但气候模型显示，它们将引发更多极端天气事件——比如热浪和强风暴。”
